title: Pullman's garden lodge: its rounded corner, balcony and columns
items: The small stone lodge beside the Pullman conservatory, across 18th Street from the house, now looks more like the 1894 Inland Architect plate. Its upper storey turns the north-east corner on a gentle curve, and the roof's edge flares out and down over that corner. A balcony with an open balustrade runs above the porch and curves round at its east end. Two round columns now stand between the porch's three openings, where there had been flat piers.
The lead deck on top of the roof is now ringed by open ironwork with a tall spire at each corner, as the plate shows, instead of plain posts and a rail.
The curve's exact plan, the balcony's depth and its balusters cannot be measured from the plate, so they are recorded as reconstructions.
